blocking_findings.title: TRANSACTION_AUTHORIZATION_V7 replacement program targets a nonexistent effective-base field
blocking_findings.evidence: Replacement program 19 operation 5 invokes REPLACE_FIELD_DESCRIPTOR_INLINE for root_access_attestation. The exact corrected effective TRANSACTION_AUTHORIZATION_V6 base has 28 fields and no root_access_attestation; that name exists only in V6's explicitly non-effective typed descriptor-source body. The base guard requires one existing target and therefore discards the entire registry. Minimal successor repair: use a guarded ADD operation with exact absent precondition, anchor, placement, and displayed descriptor, or bind an exact existing access field; never source the field implicitly from the non-effective body.

blocking_findings.title: Dotted-source qualification does not define unique canonical registry bytes
blocking_findings.evidence: The traversal and 31 source-resolution rows are mechanically complete, but the construction contract never says whether each descriptor preserves source_token with an out-of-band binding or replaces it in-place with qualified_token. It also freezes no replacement direction or pre/post offset domain. Both interpretations resolve every pointer yet produce different canonical registry and Root projection hashes. Minimal successor repair: explicitly choose byte-preserving out-of-band bindings, or freeze a complete in-place right-to-left replacement algorithm with pre/post pointer and offset semantics, then bind and independently recompute the final bytes.

blocking_findings.title: ILLEGAL_SPLIT_STATE cannot instantiate or close a schema-valid incident
blocking_findings.evidence: ILLEGAL_SPLIT_STATE remains preauthorized, but every incident-evidence presence row is keyed to one of fourteen legal failure adjacencies and INCIDENT_RECEIPT_V7 requires selection by the joined legal adjacency row. An illegal partition has no such row. The only closed-state predicate additionally requires illegal_partition_boolean=false, so closeout would erase the evidence that triggered the incident. Minimal successor repair: add typed illegal-partition incident presence modes independent of legal adjacency, deterministic conservative branch/flush/P4/quarantine evidence rules, and a closeout predicate that preserves and validates the illegal evidence rather than falsifying it.

blocking_findings.title: P2 rename and quarantine-rename failures lack a truthful flush-evidence mode
blocking_findings.evidence: After every pre-rename flush succeeds, a P2 terminal rename failure leaves a strict successful prefix stopped by a non-flush operation: 8 rows for SUCCESS, 6 for FAILURE_NO_QUARANTINE, or 7 for FAILURE_WITH_QUARANTINE. The inherited execution schema permits only NOT_ENTERED, FIRST_FAILURE_PREFIX ending in a non-successful flush observation, or COMPLETE_SUCCESS. Failed or uncertain quarantine rename is also excluded because WITH_QUARANTINE plan selection presumes successful quarantine rename. Minimal successor repair: add an exact SUCCESSFUL_PREFIX_STOPPED_BY_INTERVENING_OPERATION mode joined to the raw rename observation, attempted count and next index; define deterministic quarantine-rename failure selection/evidence and incident routing.

blocking_findings.title: P5 external completion artifact has no independent durable readback witness
blocking_findings.evidence: The external observation explicitly does not attest its own close/readback. Consumer grants give metadata and CREATE_NEW write authority but zero read-after-write paths, and no distinct downstream authority exact-opens, hashes, or canonically validates the finalized observation. A short, corrupt, or unclosed write can therefore be indistinguishable from the claimed P5 completion event. Minimal successor repair: grant a distinct preauthorized downstream authority exact read/readback of each external observation and require a typed post-write snapshot, byte/hash/canonical validation, and fail-closed incident route, or bind completion to an existing later independently validated artifact without a self-cycle.
